newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks rise to close higher after quiet day.
newsitem.headline: French stocks rise to close higher after quiet day.

text.p: French shares rose at the end of the trading session, lifted by a firm opening on Wall St to recapture all the ground they lost on Tuesday, leaving the market in slightly bullish shape, dealers said.
"We recovered all of yesterday's loss," said one trader. "Not a bad day, actually."
But dealers said the trading was calm and without real impetus in either direction.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 11.24 points or 0.5 percent at 2,240.05. The CAC-40 futures contract was up nine points at 2,244.0. Volume was 4.9 billion francs.

Eurotunnel closed off 1.28 percent at 7.70 francs, up from its low of 7.55 francs earlier. The share was hit after an overnight fire in the Channel tunnel injured 34 people and forced the tunnel to close.

Euro Disney closed down 0.44 percent at 11.40 francs after falling as far as 10.80 francs during the day. The company reported profits of 202 million francs for the 1995/96 year, the top end of expectations, but forecast a tough 1997.
Elf was in the spotlight with heavy trading. The share closed up 2.19 percent at 438.80 francs on positive sentiment.
"Everyone realises it's a very cheap stock," said a dealer. "It's still offering very good yield. The company has been restructured and looks like it has its house in order."
Axime and Sligos were big gainers, up 4.24 percent and 3.35 percent respectively, in the afterglow of an agreed merger and due to arbitrage plays on the stocks.
French insurer Axa ended the session up 1.35 percent at 301.0 francs after French regulators approved its merger with rival Unions des Assurances de Paris (UAP).
UAP closed up 1.2 percent. UAP and Axa were the stocks with the second and third highest turnover on the day.

Insurer GAN ended down 2.98 percent at 114.0 francs, off its low for the day of 109 francs, reached shortly after the open. The share was hit by investor reaction to a battle between the government and the company's chairman over the privatisation of GAN's banking unit CIC.
CIC shares closed down 1.25 percent at 317.0 francs.
Canal Plus was off 0.48 percent at 1,233 francs after a French court dismissed a court case by broadcaster TF1 against the pay-TV station. TF1 shares closed 0.19 percent higher at 536 francs.
